pr.title: Run release candidate checks in trusted CI and stabilize goal smoke
pr.body:
## Summary

A triggered server release can stop because its token-created PR needs separate workflow approval. The database check also fails when the goal-pace smoke backdates a goal and unintentionally makes an older fixture goal active.

Cut release now calls the existing read-only validation workflows with explicit candidate and source SHAs. Both merge gates verify their results in the same trusted run, preserving exact refs, canonical release mirrors, merge-tree checks and publication dependencies. The smoke keeps one explicit active-goal identity through its timezone, Wear and import cases. Normal PR/manual validation and the release-only platform/rollback skips remain intact.

Closes #457. This is a master-based follow-on; PR441/452 and immutable release PR455 are unchanged. Overlapping workflow changes need coordinated integration before those separate branches advance.

## Test plan and behavior evidence

This changes release tooling and a synthetic database fixture, with no application UI flow. [Retained evidence and exact source/scope](https://github.com/MChartier/calibrate-health/blob/6bdfa677ae1b892d7cb147c2be7d271b896143d6/README.md):

| Scenario | Expected and observed |
| --- | --- |
| Run the unchanged goal smoke on disposable PostgreSQL, then run the corrected fixture | The original fails with 90,000 instead of 84,000. The corrected smoke retains the expected weights and passes all subsequent timezone, Wear, import, concurrency and receipt-replay cases. |
| Supply trusted-run CI fixtures, including no PR-event runs | The five required validation surfaces pass only with exact source/run/candidate bindings. Missing, failed, cancelled and wholly skipped checks reject finalization. |
| Retry validation or move a ref while inspecting it | Same-run, same-candidate successes may be reused; a newer failure overrides older success. Changed master, candidate, run attempt or workflow source rejects both initial and premerge checks. |

## Supporting checks and limitations

The maintained release suite passed **160 tests with 2 existing skips**; its focused CI/workflow subset passed **60 tests**. Release consistency and diff checks passed. The actual red/green database run used Windows, Node24.19.0, Prisma7.9.0 and PostgreSQL16.14; [All five hosted workflows passed](https://github.com/MChartier/calibrate-health/actions?query=branch%3Afix%2Frelease-candidate-ci-457), including the [PostgreSQL15 upgrade, complete goal smoke and rollback checks](https://github.com/MChartier/calibrate-health/actions/runs/37885538676). CI retains its existing Node and PostgreSQL configurations.

Raw actionlint1.7.12 still reports unsupported `job.workflow_sha` and `queue: max` features already used by the repository. Filtering only those diagnostics yields no other errors; no repository suppression was added.

Source `0c9c839e`, actual target/source merge-base `547206a1`; [one commit and all 12 changed paths](https://github.com/MChartier/calibrate-health/blob/6bdfa677ae1b892d7cb147c2be7d271b896143d6/scope.json). Original failure logs and artifact digests remain on the nonmerged evidence ref. The trusted release path was not dispatched: no merge, release, provider operation or deployment is claimed. Independent QA remains required. The configured review bot previously refused solely for quota; no new bot completion or retry is claimed.

commit.message:
Keep new goal baseline aligned with same-day weight corrections (#449)

## Summary

Saving or correcting today's weight after creating a goal could leave
its starting weight stale. Web/mobile, Wear and imported weights now
align the current goal's baseline within their weight transaction,
preserving goal identity, start day, target, pace and history. The goal
sync event includes the final safety-review state.

The existing goal start day (`created_at` in the account timezone),
metric date and acceptance-local day must match. The timezone is reread
after acquiring the shared planning lock; competing weight writers take
that lock before metric rows. A late first offline replay saves its
metric without changing an older baseline, while committed retries
retain their original result.

Closes #446.

## Test plan

| Scenario | Expected and observed result | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Create a 90 kg goal, save 85 kg that day, reload Progress | The same
goal starts at 85 kg with 0% progress. Before retained 90 kg / 33%;
After shows the correction. | Matched browser captures below; maintained
metric regression. |
| Save weight before goal creation, or while goal creation holds the
planning lock | Both orders establish the new baseline without changing
target, pace, date or completed food-day history. | PostgreSQL smoke. |
| Change timezone while a weight writer waits; test LA/UTC in both
directions with explicit/default dates | Eligibility and default date
use the committed timezone, and retries retain the receipt. | Forced
PostgreSQL overlap and controlled-clock route tests. |
| Overlap web and Wear weight writes in both orders | No lock inversion;
successful same-day writes correct the baseline and sync it once. Stale
Wear revisions return 409; historical Wear writes retain the baseline.
Wear parses date syntax first; the locked timezone decides eligibility
in both directions. Newly future dates are rejected without
metric/baseline/sync writes; newly current dates are accepted and
correct the baseline. | Forced PostgreSQL overlap. |
| Import a current-day weight, overwrite it, KEEP it, or repeat a
historical/identical import | Only accepted current-day weight writes
correct the baseline. KEEP, historical rows and identical repeats
produce no extra goal correction events. After a concurrent timezone
change, accepted/skipped rows, counts and future warnings use the locked
account day. | Actual import route and ZIP parser in PostgreSQL smoke. |
| Replay after midnight, retry after a newer correction, use pounds,
fail sync or make a plan unsafe | No historical/stale overwrite;
canonical precision, atomic rollback and existing safety-review behavior
are preserved. | Maintained backend regressions. |

Validation: 61 targeted backend tests passed during the writer-path
fixes; the final affected Wear suite (14 tests), import suite (6 tests)
and backend typecheck passed after their narrow follow-ups.
[Current-head PostgreSQL validation
passed](https://github.com/MChartier/calibrate-health/actions/runs/37828422760),
including all concurrency and both-direction timezone cases. All
current-head hosted checks passed: 10 successful, 14 path-filtered
skips. [Configured review completed with no major
issues](https://github.com/MChartier/calibrate-health/pull/449#issuecomment-6067011549)
at this head; all seven prior findings have verified dispositions and
resolved threads. Earlier unchanged-client validation passed 35 client
tests, both Expo builds and two browser captures; those unaffected
suites were not repeated. Native device testing is deferred.
[Independent
QA](https://github.com/MChartier/calibrate-health/pull/449#issuecomment-6067634380)
passed code, review dispositions, applicable CI and evidence checks;
final description reassessment remains pending.

The screenshots show a synthetic API correction followed by the actual
Progress UI reload. They use the real metric route with synthetic
persistence; unrelated trend/target/projection values are fixtures. They
do not establish native or real database behavior.

Actual target master is `9dc0739e36168aa273530fe00ae5f85fb9c8a3fe` after
PR436 merged. Historical merge-base and captured Before:
`4cbcbc740fbe5fa5646b4de31951c79a653176d5`. Captured After:
`eb142dd0bcc527398e83b91d29d4514fd9b4e516`. Current head:
`650862e1c13be66fe5ec05495320cc66ac32f8bb`. Later fixes preserve the
captured stable-timezone scenario; the old images are not relabeled as
new-head captures. The [independent target-impact
assessment](https://github.com/MChartier/calibrate-health/blob/124f0906831b6d97ea09463ca3b4a1f0f6a95ab3/verdict.json)
found PR436's incoming changes integrate without textual conflict and
preserve the goal-baseline behavior and original capture applicability.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: stale 90 kg
baseline](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MChartier/calibrate-health/ce02f46f2d6b3794d3911a74a7c29a63ac6960c4/before.png)
| ![After: corrected 85 kg
baseline](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MChartier/calibrate-health/ce02f46f2d6b3794d3911a74a7c29a63ac6960c4/after.png)
|

[Original captures, build manifests and immutable
provenance](https://github.com/MChartier/calibrate-health/tree/ce02f46f2d6b3794d3911a74a7c29a63ac6960c4)
and [final source binding, review-fix evidence and capture
applicability](https://github.com/MChartier/calibrate-health/blob/458ff9fa117ca51b2c07c565069d809ecb8518d5/final-source-binding.md)
are retained outside product history. All earlier evidence records
remain accessible. Implementation-owner and independent QA pixel
inspection completed; the independent assessment verified original
provenance and current-source/target applicability. [The previous
description](https://github.com/MChartier/calibrate-health/pull/449#issuecomment-6067666764)
is preserved.

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,28 @@
+# Same-day goal starting weight
+
+A weight entered or corrected on the current goal's first local day also corrects
+its starting weight. The goal ID, start day, target, pace and calorie-plan history
+stay intact. Weights retain the existing tenth-of-a-unit input precision and
+canonical gram storage. An unsafe corrected plan uses the existing review state;
+the correction does not silently change its target or pace.
+
+The existing model has no separate start-date field. The start day is the local
+date of `Goal.created_at` in the user's timezone, as used by Progress and
+calibration. Correction requires that start day, the metric's date and the current
+user-local day all match after acquiring the calorie-planning lock.
+The timezone is reread inside that transaction after the lock, so a profile
+change that commits first determines eligibility and the default metric date.
+Wear and import weight writers acquire the same guard before metric rows to
+avoid reversing the lock order against normal corrections.
+Accepted Wear writes and imported current-day weights use the same correction
+and goal-sync rule. Imports that KEEP an existing weight, body-fat-only updates
+and historical import rows do not change the baseline.
+
+Offline weight intent remains `{ weight, date }` plus its stable operation ID.
+Until accepted, the app shows the pending metric and retains the server-owned
+goal; calorie targets/projections remain marked as syncing. Replay refreshes the
+goal query. A first replay after the start day saves the metric but leaves the
+older baseline unchanged: there is no verified original-submission day in this
+protocol. Retrying an already committed operation returns its original receipt
+without overwriting later corrections. Historical edits, body-fat-only updates
+and other goals are not baseline corrections.

issue.title: Validate release candidates without manual CI approval and stabilize goal-pace smoke
issue.body:
## Problem

The [release candidate CI gate](https://github.com/MChartier/calibrate-health/actions/runs/37880190066/job/113658571223) stopped on approval-required checks for bot-created PR455. GitHub now requires maintainer approval for pull-request runs created by the repository token, so the current pipeline cannot complete unattended after the human triggers it.

A separately retried [database check](https://github.com/MChartier/calibrate-health/actions/runs/37880437998/job/113665062675?pr=455) passed all 48 migrations but failed the goal-pace concurrency smoke: 90,000 observed versus 84,000 expected. Source inspection indicates a date-dependent synthetic active-goal fixture, requiring disposable-PostgreSQL confirmation.

## Requirements and acceptance

- Reuse existing CI validation in the trusted release workflow on the exact candidate SHA, without a new token, protection change or routine human workflow approval. Fail closed on missing, failed, cancelled or wholly skipped required validation.
- Preserve current source/head checks, canonical release-only transformation, merge-tree verification, required check coverage and existing platform/rollback skip policy. Validation receives read-only permissions and no publication/provider credentials.
- Make the goal-pace fixture deterministic without weakening expected behavior or changing production goal semantics unless reproduction demonstrates a product defect. Cover all later timezone, Wear and import races.
- Preserve normal PR CI behavior and add proportionate maintained regression coverage for candidate identity, failure gating and the date-sensitive fixture.
- No live release rerun, immutable PR455/candidate edit, merge, tag, publication, provider, credential or protection-setting action.

## Implementation plan

From verified current master, reproduce the smoke failure on disposable synthetic PostgreSQL, correct fixture identity/order, and verify the complete smoke. Refactor the release's existing validation entrypoints for explicit candidate/source identity rather than pull-request event assumptions; check both initial and final premerge gates. Coordinate overlapping workflow/test/documentation files with PR441/452 owners, preserving their branches and evidence. Publish one focused draft fix with current-head CI and independent QA; describe any separately required operational recovery without executing it.

## Implementing Codex task

Sole implementation owner: verified task `01a11db5-8540-740a-a673-1026c0b90007`.

## Implementing PR

Current draft: [#458](https://github.com/MChartier/calibrate-health/pull/458), with native `Closes #457` linkage. PR441/452 and immutable release PR455 remain separate and unchanged.

Authority: the user requested hands-off release progression after triggering it, then explicitly said on October 9, “Let's fix the CI job and the pipeline defintiion together.” This authorizes the bounded code correction, not release execution or security-setting changes.

Preserve all required validation surfaces, justified release-only skips, final identity checks and fail-closed publication dependencies.
